label: copy-phase input b/d/v/f while outputting d/v (mostly first copy step of short sequences)
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.016% of steps). About 90% of its activation mass is in the copy phase and 60% at recall_idx 1, where the input is the fed-back first original token. It is concentrated on short sequences (L=3-4) and on inputs b/d/f/v (b alone carries 49% of mass) with output d or v (d carries 51%). Typical top examples are b d x y <DEL> [b] d x. But the feature fires on only a small fraction of steps that match these conditions: in_tok in {b,d,f,v} with out_tok in {d,v} in the copy phase has about 2% precision. Restricting to recall_idx 1 and L<=5 raises precision to about 21%, but recall drops to about 30%. There is also a tail outside this pattern: about 10% of mass is in the original phase (e.g. e/f/1/j at t=5-6), plus later copy steps with input b. Next-output and other history variables did not separate firing from non-firing cases. Magnitude is highest for b->d at the first copy step of L=4 sequences. It never fires at t<3 or on the delimiter step. No predicate got above F1 0.25 on dev.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: b, f, d, v, e, j; least: p, l, q, n) and the token being output (most: d, v, u, b, a, k; least: n, y, x, l); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=4, t=6.
